issues.detail: Objection 1 states the agreement was executed on 'stamp paper of Rs. 100 only (Clause 12)' — this is supported by the client's own words (Clause 12). However, Objection 2 states 'the applicable law caps the security deposit at two months' rent (Rule MTA-11). The permissible cap on this basis would be [TO CONFIRM]' — the drafter then computes in next_steps '2 months x Rs. 50,000' as if confirmed. The draft body itself uses [TO CONFIRM] correctly, but next_steps item 3 states 'Supervising advocate to verify the statutory security deposit cap calculation (2 months x Rs. 50,000)' — this is procedurally fine as a note, not a stated fact in the notice body. No issue here.
issues.fix: No change needed — retained for reviewer awareness only; [TO CONFIRM] is used correctly in the draft body.

issues.detail: Demand item 1 states 'i.e., by **[TO CONFIRM]**' — this is a deadline date that should either be computed from the notice date (20 September 2026 + 15 days = 5 October 2026) or marked [TO CONFIRM]. The literal '[TO CONFIRM]' is permitted, so this is allowed. However, there is no issue to flag here per the rules.
issues.fix: No change needed — [TO CONFIRM] is an explicitly permitted placeholder.

issues.detail: next_steps item 7 states 'Consider filing an application before the Rent Controlling Authority under MPACA-7 for fixation of standard rent' — 'MPACA-7' is cited as a section id in next_steps but is NOT present in the SECTIONS JSON slice and is not cited in the draft's `sections` array.
issues.fix: Remove 'MPACA-7' from next_steps item 7 or replace with '[TO CONFIRM — rule id to be verified by supervising advocate]'; do not cite a section id not present in the SECTIONS slice.

issues.detail: Section TPA-108 is cited in `sections` with why: 'Clauses 9 and 11 jointly breach the Lessor's statutory duties of quiet enjoyment and structural maintenance.' The gist of TPA-108 covers quiet enjoyment and the lessee's right to make repairs neglected by the lessor and deduct cost from rent — it does not state that the lessor has a duty of structural maintenance as a positive obligation that cannot be excluded by contract. The `why` overstates the gist by asserting structural maintenance is a non-excludable statutory duty of the lessor, which the gist does not support.
issues.fix: Revise the `why` for TPA-108 to: 'Clauses 9 and 11 breach the Lessor's duty to allow quiet enjoyment and the Lessee's statutory right to carry out repairs neglected by the Lessor and deduct their reasonable cost from rent, as provided by TPA-108.' Remove the characterisation that structural repair liability is a non-excludable statutory duty of the Lessor, as the gist does not support that claim.

issues.detail: Objection 8 (Clause 11) in draft_markdown states: 'A blanket exclusion of the Lessor's liability for all structural repairs is unenforceable.' The gist of TPA-108 provides only that the lessee may carry out repairs neglected by the lessor and deduct reasonable cost from rent — it does not state that structural repair liability is non-excludable or that a blanket contractual exclusion is unenforceable. This is a legal conclusion not supported by the gist of TPA-108.
issues.fix: Replace 'A blanket exclusion of the Lessor's liability for all structural repairs is unenforceable.' with 'To the extent TPA-108 preserves the Lessee's right to carry out repairs neglected by the Lessor and deduct their reasonable cost from rent, any clause purporting to exclude that right entirely may be unenforceable — this is to be confirmed by the supervising advocate.'
